boundaries: Derived Refresh is not Representation Revision because canonical machine bytes remain unchanged.
Projection validation is evidence, not approval.
A changed generator may require a separate tooling decision but does not turn its outputs into semantic authority.
claim_ceiling: This candidate defines derived refresh semantics only. It does not regenerate any current projection, adopt a generator, or authorize tooling changes.

scope.applicability: Deterministic regeneration of noncanonical projections from unchanged canonical machine state.
exclusions: Generator changes treated as implicitly adopted tooling authority.

examples: Regenerate DEFINITIONS-INDEX.md from an unchanged registry.
Regenerate CONTEXT.md from an unchanged context.json without creating a context epoch.
domain_context.explanation: DEFINITION.md, CONTEXT.md, indexes, and reverse Context Map membership views are generated surfaces. Rebuilding them from unchanged canonical JSON is a Derived Refresh.

plain_language.explanation: Rebuilding a human or lookup view from unchanged canonical data. It should be checked, but it does not ask the semantic owner to approve the same meaning again.

boundary_conditions: If canonical machine bytes change, the operation is not a Derived Refresh.
Generated output cannot redefine canonical meaning.
A generator change follows its own tooling workflow and does not silently gain adoption.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: DerivedRefresh(x,g,y) iff CanonicalInputDigest(x) unchanged and y = DeterministicGenerate(g,x) and Projection(y) and AuthorityEffect(y)=none. DerivedRefresh does not imply SemanticEpoch or RepresentationRevision.
scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Derived Refresh is the deterministic regeneration and validation of a noncanonical projection from an unchanged canonical machine input under an exact generator binding. It records the canonical input digest, generator identity and digest, output digest, parity result, and validation receipt. A Derived Refresh creates no Semantic Epoch, Representation Revision, Governance Decision, or authority effect. A change to the generator is governed separately as a tooling change even when refreshing its outputs has no semantic effect.
testable_conditions: The canonical input digest is unchanged.
Two renders with the same generator and input are byte-identical.
The output declares generated-only posture and authority_effect none.
